corrections.contract_gain_bound_erratum: audio-replay-v3.md originally wrote g <= 1 next to control[31:16] <= 32768 (Q4.12), which is 8.0 not 1.0; B found it (67d28b2). The contract now states g <= 8 with the 41-bit argument (|w| <= 2^24 and g <= 8 give g*w <= 2^39 < 2^40-1), so the arithmetic conclusion is unchanged and only the stated range was wrong. The deployed bitstream is unaffected because the working gain was 1631. The RTL comment at audio_pl_replay.v:195 still carries the old "gain is <= 1.0" wording; it was deliberately NOT edited after the build so that the source that produced bitstream 48e38f78 stays identifiable, and the imprecision is registered here instead.
corrections.board_offline_2026_10_27: after the field window the board stopped answering on 192.168.2.99:22, so the current-fixture |H| peak scan and the distance ladder below could not be run; no measurement is claimed for either.
corrections.bit22_stop_semantics: earlier text in this file said bit22 was an evidence field that did not change the stop condition. That is no longer true and has been overwritten: the captain authorised making input full scale a stop condition, so "input overload is visible" and "input overload stops the run" are now two separate facts that must not be merged. The contract audio-replay-v3.md carries the table.
corrections.gain_unit_wording: audio-replay-v3.md used "round_Q12" and "Q4.12" without defining them. The gain word is control[31:16], unsigned 16-bit with 12 fractional bits (Q4.12, 0..8.0); the coefficients are 24-bit Q20. The contract now states this explicitly and uses round_shift12().

coupling_table.how: closed-loop boost at the |H| peak = 1/(1-g*|H|); this is what raises the microphone level when g goes up, and it is the constraint that binds before stability does

consequences: -4 dB is ABOVE the bypass critical gain (-4.40 dB): g*|H| = 1.047, so it howls with no cancellation at all. B's 'try -6 / -4' must stop at -6 dB.
raising g by 2 dB (from -8 to -6) raises the closed-loop output at the peak by about 6.1 dB (9.39 -> 15.48 dB), i.e. about 3 dB of microphone headroom lost per 1 dB of g

measured at 20 cm with g = -8: closed-loop microphone peaks of -23.1 and -8.5 dBFS on two takes of the same sentence. The second is 2.5 dB above the -6 dBFS rule already at g = -8, so at 20 cm the gain cannot go up at all; -6 dB needs roughly twice the distance

distance alone does not set the peak: two takes at the same 20 cm and the same arm differ by 14.6 dB, so any distance ladder must be repeated per take and gated on the measured peak and bit22, not on the nominal distance

correction_to_B_option_2.B_said: lowering the Codec ADC gain by k equals lowering g, so it is wasted effort
correction_to_B_option_2.why_that_is_incomplete: it is a headroom move, not a gain move. Scaling the ADC by k and the coefficients by k, then the digital gain by 1/k, gives out = (g/k)(k*m - k*p) = g*(m - p): identical loop gain and identical playback level, but the microphone path no longer saturates. The coefficient scaling is exact (B says so himself), so no refit is needed. The point is to stop destroying input information at 12 cm, which no digital stage can undo.
correction_to_B_option_2.cost: identity has to be re-registered (scaled coefficients) and the ADC gain is a calibrated parameter
